extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers and journalists covering wartime events and the International Food Conference (Hot Springs)
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper news-article (AP dispatch) reporting on wartime military actions, casualty lists, and rules/access for reporters covering an international food conference at Hot Springs. It combines battlefield dispatches, government/political developments, and press-access procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press access restrictions at International Food Conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsmen were effectively barred today from the hotel where the International Food Conference opens Tuesday ... Military police, 200 of them, were thrown around the hotel grounds as part of the Government's decision prevent reporters from attending all but opening and closing sessions of the two-week conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State Department representatives said newsmen could do these things: 1. Use as a press room the Casino (transformed to a pressroom for the duration of the food parley). 2. To go horseback riding on the grounds. 3. To attend nightly movies in the hotel (their journey to and from the theater will be along a specified route not permitting them to meet or mingle with delegates in the hotel). By telephone, request any delegate to go down to the Casino for a conference or an interview, if the delegate is willing. Reporters will be admitted to plenary session of the conference Tuesday at 9 P. M. but from that opening session until the final session about the night of June 3 newsmen will be barred from any sessions or sectional meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter accreditation and numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Forty-five newsmen, including two from magazines, eleven photographers and five radio correspondents have been accredited to the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About fifteen of them arrived earlier and were quartered in various small hotels or private homes in the neighborhood of the hotel; reporters are barred from the hotel proper and expected to use the Casino pressroom and specified routes when attending permitted events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference security and delegate housing protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: All the delegates will live and work under the same roof—a contrast with League of Nations meetings—so the Homestead Hotel houses delegates from forty-three nations and the members of the conference secretariat. About 200 soldiers have the task of keeping intruders out of the conference grounds; of this garrison 139 are quartered in the 600-room hotel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference logistics emphasize seclusion and self-sufficiency (hotel has own fields, dairy, airport, etc.) and strict control of access; press movement and contact with delegates are limited by military police and State Department routing/permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senator O'Mahoney's proposed rule for trade-agreement approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Senator O'Mahoney said his proposed amendment would prohibit any trade agreement from becoming effective until it had been approved by Congress 'in the same manner and form' by which legislative approval is required in the country with which the agreement is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: Legislation renewing the reciprocal-trade authority was passed by the House (which rejected a proposal enabling Congress to reject any agreement within 90 days). O'Mahoney argued that without submission to Congress the people's representatives would be excluded from post-war economic reorganization; he intends to offer the amendment to test Congressional sentiment. He noted that of some thirty-odd agreements now in effect all but four became operative without action by foreign legislative bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria cited for military decorations/commendations (Bismarck Sea/low-level operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crews were cited for 'courage, skill' for actions such as a reconnaissance crew shadowing a Japanese convoy for five hours during daylight, sending back reports constantly so other planes could find and bomb the ships, and another heavy bomber crew that 'bombed and strafed searchlight and anti-aircraft batteries' at Lakunai Air-drome, Rabaul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of behavior meriting citation include prolonged low-level reconnaissance under danger, continuous reporting enabling follow-on strikes, and direct attacks on enemy shore defenses/searchlights/AA batteries. The article uses these specific mission examples to illustrate why certain airmen were decorated (e.g., Corporal William S. Bates).
